OBJECT_FORCE (Phase 040): objects as arms. Any discrete object a resident holds in a hand can be swung (the strike action, with) or thrown (the throw action). What the object does comes from its physical data: ITEMS weight, the material's hardness and fragility (MATERIALS), whether a container, and whether its kind is edged (TOOL_FIT edged_kinds, with the cutting verbs of TOOL_FIT edge_verbs). There is no weapon list and no weapon skill; the skill is `fighting`. Switch: physical_subsystems.object_force (default off). With the switch off, a strike ignores `with` and a throw is refused as unsupported, so the simple village is unchanged.

STRIKE WITH AN OBJECT. The blow's power is the bare-hand power of Phase 038 (attacker force x (1 + technique_weight x skill)) times the object's strike multiplier. A TOOL_FIT row for the verb `strike` (an authored fitness, for example a knife's) is used as it is, with its effort. Otherwise the multiplier is harm_scale x weight_term x hardness_term (no edge bonus on a blow). A load heavier than unwieldy_above x the user's effective strength is clumsy: the multiplier is divided by the ratio of load to limit, and the stamina cost is multiplied by that ratio (capped at RESOLUTION effort_cap). A tool that lands a blow wears through the usual tool wear; one that breaks on impact is destroyed (breakage below).

THROW. The throw action sends a held object along the grid line toward a target cell or resident. Range is range_base x effective strength x intensity, divided by the object's weight over weight_reference (at least 1, so light objects do not travel further than the reference), at most range_max cells. The flight stops before any cell of the sight occluders on the line (Phase 028) and at the end of its range. A target beyond range, or behind an obstacle, is not reached: the object lands short or before the obstacle, and nothing is refused. A throw that reaches a resident is a contest: the thrower's aim is (1 + technique_weight x skill) x exhaustion step x distance falloff x intensity accuracy, where the distance falloff is 1 / (1 + distance / distance_reference) and the accuracy is 1 / (1 + accuracy_intensity_loss x (intensity - 1)) above intensity 1. A target that does not step aside is hit when the aim reaches passive_defence. A target that evades (the offered `evade` reaction, when it is eligible) is hit only if its own evade defence, (1 + technique_weight x skill) x exhaustion step, falls short of the aim. A hit does throw_harm x thrown multiplier x intensity x distance falloff x hit quality (from the margin of aim against defence, scaled to 0 to 1), from cause violence; the object falls on the target's cell. A miss lands on the first open cell beside the target's cell (in sorted order), where the object can be picked up. The stamina cost and the strain are the resolution core's, on a demand of weight over throw_demand_unit. Nothing here is random.

BREAKAGE. An object breaks on impact (an obstacle or a person it hits) when its material's fragility (MATERIALS) is at least any_fragility, or when it is a container and the fragility is at least container_fragility. A broken object is destroyed: the item is conserved or destroyed by breaking, never minted. A thrown object that misses and lands on open ground does not break.

APPROX: every number here is a model choice. None is measured or sourced. The reference object is the hammer (ITEMS weight 1.0, metal). throw_harm is set to the scale of the Phase 038 blow (strike_harm 0.1 x blow power 1.2 = 0.12), so that a thrown reference object at distance 0 does what a full unarmed blow does. The sign of each relation (heavier and harder harms more; range falls with weight; accuracy falls with distance and with intensity) is the physical claim the tests check; the magnitudes are chosen to be of the right order.

KEYS. harm_scale: the multiplier of a metal reference object's blow relative to a bare-hand blow (a hammer strikes twice as hard as a fist). weight_reference: the ITEMS weight of the reference object. weight_exponent: harm grows as the weight ratio to the reference raised to this power (0.5: diminishing returns). weight_term_min, weight_term_max: the clamp on that term. hardness_reference: the MATERIALS hardness of the reference material (metal, 0.6); hardness_term is the material's hardness over it, clamped to [0, 2]. unknown_hardness: the hardness of an object whose material is not in MATERIALS (unknown is soft). edge_bonus: the extra multiplier of an edged kind thrown or swung with a cutting verb (TOOL_FIT edge_verbs). throw_harm: the harm of a reference object thrown at distance 0 at intensity 1 with a full hit. throw_demand_unit: the weight in ITEMS units that the throw's demand counts as 1.0 (an average adult's effort per unit). range_base, range_max: the range in cells of a reference object (APPROX). distance_reference: the distance at which aim and harm fall to half. accuracy_intensity_loss: the share of aim lost per unit of intensity above 1. passive_defence: the defence of a target that does not step aside, in aim units. unwieldy_above: the weight a person can swing per unit of effective strength before the swing is clumsy. container_fragility, any_fragility: the breakage thresholds on MATERIALS fragility.
